analysis:
Examined all supplied patches, BASE/HEAD excerpts and file metadata against the definition index and supplied T-041 detail. SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift:119-219 introduces lock-protected shared/exclusive leases. Admission preserves queued-writer priority; cancellation removes waiters and admits newly eligible readers; release removes the actual holder; upgrade requires sole ownership and no waiters. Continuations resume outside the lock. No concrete coordinator regression was identified. Maintenance.swift:29-39 forwards optional unusedSince while retaining root ownership, removal locking and reconciliation; scans still acquire exclusive nonblocking leases at :146. Read.swift HEAD patch :129/:204 changes initial and retry reads to shared leases. BASE :117-223 shows scratch reservation, cancellation/epoch checks, unwind and refund paths retained by this patch.
Relevant concerns are T-041/A-001/TB-007 cache authentication, sliding TTL, transient memory accounting and availability (A-018). No supplied change alters scope-derived lookup keys, encryption, authorization, billing or plaintext exposure. Concurrent reads are new behavior, but their safety depends on readAttempt and related mutation paths not supplied here. Integration should examine whether corruption deletion, mtime refresh, parent-chain reads and file/index updates obtain appropriate exclusive access or safely handle upgrade refusal; Maintenance.swift:114-124 itself does not acquire a file lease, so its caller contract matters. Also verify SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove enforces unusedSince under the lease with refreshed access timestamps, and concurrent restore buffers/import plans remain charged to the process budget. These missing implementations are coverage limits, not demonstrated vulnerabilities. T-041's description of a shared staging reservation should be reconciled with actual concurrent restore accounting. No supported finding in this source scope; material cross-file contracts remain unresolved.
